character.name: Sebak
character.title: The Crow in the Wind
character.lineage: Half-Uchiha (Son of Uchiha Itachi) / Unknown Maternal Bloodline

alar.notes: 1 firm Alar binding in combat (scales with Intelligence and University training)

features.name: Body Flicker (Shunshin)
features.description: Teleport/dash up to 30 ft. to an unoccupied space you can see without provoking opportunity attacks.

features.name: Chakra-Fuelled Link
features.description: Act as a pure, lossless thermal/kinetic source for a Sympathetic binding for 1 round, bypassing the need for a fire or the risk of Binder's Chills.

features.name: Precision Throw
features.description: Curve a thrown kunai/dagger around half or three-quarters cover, granting Advantage on the attack roll.

features.name: Setting a Binding
features.description: Bonus action to set up, whatever the link quality. Roll an Alar check: d20 + INT + proficiency, plus WIS when focused (lost if you took damage or were grappled since your last turn; advantage after a calm round of preparation). DC by link: Perfect 8, Good 11, Poor 15. A failure means slippage and a partial effect, not a miss. A binding acting on a person lets them save against your Sympathy DC. Maintaining it is free but occupies your one mental split. Shares your bonus action with Body Flicker.

features.name: Link Efficiency
features.description: Perfect Link (same piece of matter): DC 8, ~80-90%. Good Link (similar material, or blood/hair for organic targets): DC 11, ~40-60%. Poor Link (crude similarity): DC 15, ~5-15%, high slippage.

features.name: Binder's Chills
features.description: Drawing heat from your own body requires a CON save (DC 10 + energy level) or take 1d4 cold damage and 1 level of Exhaustion.

features.name: Sneak Attack (1d6)
features.description: Extra 1d6 damage when hitting with a Finesse/Ranged weapon with Advantage, or when an ally (or an active Sympathetic kinetic binding distracting the target) is within 5 ft. of the enemy.

features.name: Uchiha Dormancy (Sharingan)
features.description: The Sharingan is locked. Extreme emotional trauma or life-or-death catalysis may awaken it.

features.name: Unknown Maternal Bloodline
features.description: Passive triggers observed by the DM during high-stress physical or sympathetic events. Surrounding matter hums and vibrates. Stirred at the brink of death at the felled oak: iron and wood within reach rang and the nearest club shattered. It drained his chakra and left him exhausted. Its nature is still unknown.

items.name: Hemp rope (20 ft)
items.notes: Used to tie Pell; cut from the beam, now with Voss or in the loft

items.name: Small iron key on a cord
items.notes: Taken from the crossbowman; fits something unknown

items.name: Watch receipt for a light crossbow and 7 bolts
items.notes: Held a month at the south gate by Sergeant Voss; the crossbowman's, taken in defence of the cart

items.name: Bram's note for Rennick
items.notes: Folded twice, sealed with Bram's thumbprint in ink; says the bearer carries his box and his word and is to be paid what is due

items.name: Six bars of unknown pale metal
items.notes: Wrapped in wool inside a canvas satchel carried under Sebak's cloak (about 20 lb); carry a sympathetic link with almost no loss. A pinch has been filed off one.

items.name: Marta's note for Corwin Hale
items.notes: Introduces Sebak to Corwin Hale, a journeyman of the Medica at the University; asks him to spare a quarter of an hour

items.name: Canvas herb-gatherer's satchel
items.notes: Bought from Marta for 5 drabs; holds the six bars in wool

items.name: Voss's signed note
items.notes: Says the strongbox was inspected sealed, locked and whole at the south gate at first light on Wednesday. H. Voss, Sergeant of the Watch, with his thumbprint

keepsakes: Small wooden amulet containing a single black crow feather (mother's warning)

world.location: Imre, the south gate guardhouse, with Sergeant Voss

companions.name: Bram
companions.notes: Portly tinker driving a mule-drawn wagon from Crosson. Fever broke after midnight; weak but resting easily on a cot in the apothecary's back room. His small, iron-bound, locked strongbox is under the wagon bench, untouched; he is anxious about it.

enemies.name: Masked intruder
enemies.notes: Knocked out with a pommel strike; wakes with 1 HP in about an hour, or sooner with smelling salts or cold water. Face still wrapped.

last_log: Voss lets Sebak go and gives him a note saying the box was sealed and whole at dawn.
notes:
COSTINGS (GM reference, using the player's table of the Cealdish system). 10 drabs = 1 jot, 10 jots = 1 talent (100 drabs), 10 talents = 1 mark. Below the drab is the shim (an iron scrap by weight, ~11-14 to a drab). Compound prices like 'two and four' mean talents and jots. Benchmarks: 1 drab = casual stake, 3-4 drabs = a big meal, 5 drabs = road provisions at an Imre inn. 1 jot = Eolian cover or work aprons; 1-2 jots = a student's weekly wage; 2 jots = wagon passage; 3 jots = a sturdy second-hand cloak. 1 talent = a University term's room and board, or good shoes. 2-3 talents = average tuition. 8-10 talents = a quality steel crossbow or a master lute. Price new things in drabs and jots by default. PRICES RESET (the player agreed to a fair readjustment): barge-guard day job = 2 jots + board. Apothecary in Imre = 3 jots for the first treatment (she returned 7 jots of the talent Sebak paid, saying Sebak's field stitching saved her work), then 5 drabs/day for bed and physic, hay 2 drabs/day. Bram's promised pay for the road to Imre = a few jots wage plus about a talent as a thank-you bonus if he recovers. Sebak's looted light crossbow is ordinary, not 'quality steel': about 2-3 talents to a buyer. The player wants tuition to stay hard to afford.

STORY THREADS: Bram's strongbox (small, iron-bound, locked, heavy, under the wagon bench) and the crossbowman's iron key (scar down left cheek, aimed at Bram, patient, likely hired). Whether the key fits the strongbox is undecided; do not confirm until the player asks Bram. Voss (south gate sergeant) is sending men for the bodies; the dead brigand may be Garrick Finch (missing front tooth, left forearm tattoo) with a bounty on the roll; the fled one is heavy-set, brown patched coat, broken nose, stubble, headed east, lost his club. Crossbow and 7 bolts held by Voss for a month on a receipt.

BRAM'S ACCOUNT (told to Sebak Tuesday evening): the strongbox is not his. A thin man in grey paid him half a talent up front at his Crosson stall nine days ago, the rest due on delivery to a factor called Rennick on Gilder's Row, Imre, into his hands only. Bram never opened it; heavy for its size, no clink, 'metal in cloth, or books'. The man in grey kept the key and said Rennick would have the other; Bram must deliver it locked. Sebak's wage rides on delivery. Bram does not yet know about the crossbowman's key. Who the man in grey is, what is in the box and whether Rennick is honest are undecided; Rennick, the box and the key are linked to the ambush.

MORE FROM BRAM: never met the man in grey before. He came to Bram's Crosson stall at close of market: thin, grey cloak, hood half up, gloves, soft clerkish voice, accent from east of the river. He knew Bram's name, his mule's name and his monthly Imre run, and asked for a 'discreet' commission. Paid half a talent in clean Cealdish silver, counted out himself. Asked if Bram would travel alone; Bram said he would hire a guard; the man said 'Do as you like.' Bram suspects he only wanted him on that road on that day. Unresolved: who the man in grey is and who recommended Bram.

SEBAK TAKES THE DELIVERY: Bram gave 4 jots now and a thumb-marked note for Rennick. Balance due from Rennick on delivery is 1.5 talents; Bram promises Sebak 1 talent of it. Box and wagon are in the livery yard behind the apothecary; the girl will unlock the bench in the morning. Not moved tonight.

TRAP TUESDAY NIGHT: Sebak cut a hand's length of wax-coated twine, one end knotted to the strongbox's iron handle, the same piece of twine so a Perfect link (DC 8); Alar check 21 (adv, 15 and 7). The intruder's pull is the kinetic source, so no chakra and no Binder's Chills. It occupies his one mental split all night; it holds through ordinary sleep, frays if he is knocked out or takes a hard blow. A tug wakes him instantly.

STRONGBOX SECRETS (GM only): the crossbowman's key FITS the lock. The lid seam has an obvious strip of grey paper under a blank grey wax disc (Sebak has seen it). HIDDEN: a hair is stretched across the seam under the paper (DC 12 to spot; Sebak rolled 10 and missed it); lifting the lid breaks it and Rennick or any careful inspector will see the box was opened. The key's fit means whoever sent the crossbowman could open the box after killing Bram. Contents still undecided (heavy, muffled, metal in cloth or books).

STRONGBOX OPENED Tuesday night (Sleight 24, seal lifted whole with lamp-chimney heat and laid on Sebak's knee; it can be pressed back on). The hidden hair under the paper was broken by lifting the lid and Sebak did not notice. CONTENTS: (1) thick ledger in grey leather, strap and brass clasp, columns of names, dates and sums in a cramped shorthand; (2) about a dozen small letters tied with black thread, no names or addresses; (3) six flat hand-length bars of dull, unmarked pale metal, each wrapped in cloth, lighter than steel, heavier than tin (undecided: assay, silver alloy, a sympathy-relevant metal?). Sebak has touched nothing but the oilcloth.

THE BARS: Sebak (Investigation 17) knows they are NOT silver, tin, lead, iron or common alloys: short dull note when tapped, hard (kunai barely scores), bright scratch that does not tarnish, chills slowly in the hand. He cannot name it. Truth still undecided; an assay at the University or a sympathist could name it. Value unknown (fortune or nothing).

BARS TESTED: Sebak dropped the twine alarm to test two bars (Good link DC 11, check 17, kinetic source only). The bars carry sympathy with almost no slippage, far better than iron: a sympathist's metal, likely very valuable to a sympathist or the University. The twine alarm is NOT set at present; Sebak must re-set it (Alar DC 8) if he wants it.

LETTERS (Investigation 10, gist only): addressed only to 'R.', signed with a drawn small square; loose shorthand, no names. They discuss a consignment (the 'grey', 'the weight'), sums matching the ledger. Buyer 'will name his own price when he has seen it'; the Arcanum's clerks must not hear; 'carters are being counted at the Omethi bridge', goods must move 'by a man nobody watches'. One reply in a firmer hand (R.): 'Send it sealed and send it whole. If it comes to me opened, I will not receive it, and I will not pay.' Sebak retied the threads in the same knots. Bram was chosen as an unwatched carrier. Whether Rennick = R. is likely but undecided. The hidden hair (broken) is the 'whole' check R. will make.

LEDGER (Investigation 10, partial): about twelve rows over a year or more; each: date, six (bars), a large sum, a symbol place-mark, a word. Most 'd.' (delivered), two 'lost, recovered', one 'lost'. Last row, newest, six bars and in different ink 'tinker' with a small tick (undecided: tick means expected, or means spent). Sebak could not tell what 'lost' means (bars, carriers, or both). Clasp has a faint thumbnail scratch.

SWAP: Sebak replaced the six bars with six river stones wrapped in oilcloth (weight check Investigation 11 vs DC 12: FAILED by 1, the box is a shade lighter than it was; an attentive carrier or Rennick may notice). Bars hidden under hay in the loft corner beneath the window. Seal re-pressed (Sleight 15 vs 13, OK). The hidden hair was never found or restored (still broken). Twine alarm re-set (Alar 18 vs DC 8), occupying his one mental split.

NIGHT INTRUDER (random night roll 4): slim figure, dark clothes, hood, cloth over lower face, rag-bound boots, shuttered lantern, thin pick or blade, found the seal. Entered by the ladder hatch without Sebak or the donkey noticing; the twine alarm woke Sebak. Intruder is ten feet away at the box, back half turned, unaware Sebak is awake. Identity undecided (a hired thief, not the fled brigand). Sebak has surprise if he acts first. Not yet an encounter; set encounter.active when blows begin.

FIGHT: Sebak at 6/10 HP after the intruder's hit (4). Twine alarm still held; Sebak took damage so his Alar has no WIS bonus until his next turn passes. Intruder unnamed, a competent burglar-blade (about 12 HP, AC 13, Acrobatics +5).

TWINE ALARM DROPPED for the burning binding (mental split now used by the blood-and-flame binding on the intruder). Burning cloak near the strongbox and the hay (fire hazard, Marta forbade open flame).

INTRUDER DOWN: nonlethal, unconscious until about an hour passes (or smelling salts / cold water). Search and unmask pending. Slim, hooded, rag-bound boots, short blade (on the floor), shuttered lantern, burned cloak. Marta is awake below and calling up. Fight over; the twine alarm is NOT set. Sebak 6/10 HP, chakra 2.

PELL (the burglar, about thirty, lean, shaven, nick in one ear) interrogated Wed small hours: hired by a heavy man with broken nose, stubble, patched brown coat, bandaged hand (the fled brigand), who paid a half-talent in Cealdish silver at the Salt Barrel (cheap smoky tavern by the wharf) 'last night' and said a locked box was in the apothecary's loft with a hired blade and a tinker sleeping near it. Pell's goods: lockpicks and pry-bar, purse with five silver jots (a half-talent), tin token stamped with a barrel (credit at the Salt Barrel). Marta sent her girl for Sergeant Voss (about a quarter of an hour). Pell knows nothing more. The brigand is in Imre, probably at or near the Salt Barrel.

PELL ON HOBB: Hobb mended locks in a back room off Tallow Lane and fenced goods; small, bald, bad chest; died two winters ago. Taught Pell. Pell read the strongbox's lock: Severen work, made for the box, not bought off a shelf (whoever commissioned it had money). Voss (or watchmen) are arriving in the yard now.

VOSS ARRIVED IN THE LOFT: took Pell (to the cells; hearing before the magistrate), pocketed Pell's purse as evidence, ordered a written account from Sebak and Marta by noon, will send two men to the Salt Barrel at first light, and says the strongbox must stay where it is until he has seen it himself, open or shut. Voss has NOT inspected the box yet. The box contains six wrapped river stones; the six bars are under the hay in the loft corner by the window; the seal was lifted and replaced; the hidden hair is broken; the weight is a little light. Danger point: Voss opening the box.

DEAL FOR PELL: Sebak argued for rehabilitation (Persuasion 18 vs DC 14). Voss will hold Pell one night in the cells; tomorrow Pell shows Voss's men the heavy broken-nosed man at the Salt Barrel and swears before the magistrate; then a year's service with the watch's locksmith (mending gaol doors, teaching the watch how thieves think) for bed, board and a drab a day. Back to thieving = stocks. Marta will stitch Sebak's ribs next.

Marta stitched Sebak (six stitches, poultice), no charge; counted as spending his Hit Die (1d8+2 = 7), now HP 10/10, no Hit Dice left. Told: no lifting for two days and no bindings that need running about (flavour). Marta has asked whether the box will bring more trouble to her door. Dawn is near; Voss wants a written account by noon and to see the box. Strongbox (with stones) and bars (under hay by the loft window) are unwatched in the loft; the twine alarm is not set.

ASSAY BY MARTA (2 jots): filed a pinch from one bar. Dense, near silver but not silver; aqua fortis barely marks it; does not tarnish; in a flame it does not melt or blacken and flares once with a cool white moonlike light. Not in her assay books. Marta advises showing it quietly to someone at the University. Marta knows only that there is an unnamed metal; she did not see the bars or the box contents. Sebak filed a pinch from one bar (a little missing). One bar's filings stay with Marta's paper.

CORWIN HALE: journeyman of the Medica (six years), crosses the Omethi every second week for willow bark and poppy, careful and honest by Marta's account. Marta knows no sympathists; the Arcanum doesn't visit her shop. Marta advises: tell Hale little, and do not go to the Arcanum first.

SEBAK LEAVES MARTA'S carrying the strongbox (stones) openly in both arms and the satchel of bars under his cloak, heading for the south gate to show Voss. Voss will see the box. Risk: Voss lifts or opens it and finds stones; the seal was re-pressed, the hidden hair is broken, the weight is a little light.

VOSS EXAMINED THE BOX (no break): he walked round it, lifted one corner an inch, ran a thumb along the paper strip. His Investigation roll (3+3 = 6 vs the reseal's 15) failed: he does not notice the seal was lifted, nor the broken hair, nor the stones. He did not open it ('I will not break another man's seal without cause'). He has not noticed the weight. He asked where Sebak is taking it. Voss has Pell in the cell behind him; his men are still on the road for the bodies.

VOSS'S NOTE: he deliberately wrote what he saw (sealed, whole) and added he did not open it; he suspects Sebak is hiding something but trusts him as straight so far. Sebak told Voss only that he would deliver the box to its 'intended target'. Voss does NOT know the name Rennick. Voss expects Sebak's written account at noon.

player_notes.title: Notice by the apothecary's door
player_notes.text: Chalked on slate by the door of the apothecary's shop in Imre: "Guards wanted for river barge, Thursday. Ask at the wharf. Two jots and board." At the wharf (a short walk east of the south gate): the barge is the Wren, a long flat grain boat, tied up in the third row. Her captain is sour-faced and still counting heads; he would take me on at two jots and board. Thursday's departures are chalked on the dockmaster's post, and the dockmaster is a loud man in an oilskin cloak.

player_notes.title: Sergeant Haldric Voss, south gate watch
player_notes.text: The apothecary says to report the fight on the road to the watch at Imre's south gate and ask for Sergeant Haldric Voss by name. Big, grey-bearded, limps from an old campaign (says he got it at Vint, tells it differently each time). Likes things said plainly and in order, doesn't like being hurried. A bounty may come of it if reported today. Tell him only that I found three bandits and left. Keep quiet about the sympathy.

player_notes.title: Ask Bram about the strongbox and the key
player_notes.text: Speak to Bram about his strongbox and the small iron key. Are they related? The strongbox is small, iron-bound, locked and heavy, kept under the bench of his wagon (still untouched, and Bram was anxious about it when he woke and again at the apothecary's). The key is plain, finger-length, with a worn bow, odd teeth and no maker's mark; I took it from the scar-faced crossbowman, who aimed at Bram and not at me. Voss thinks he was hired and warned me not to show the key about Imre. Bram says (Tuesday evening, Imre): the strongbox is not his. A thin man in grey paid him half a talent up front at his stall in Crosson nine days ago, the rest due on delivery. He is to hand it, locked, to a factor called Rennick on Gilder's Row in Imre, and to nobody else. My wage comes from that payment. He never opened it. It is heavy for its size and does not clink like coin, more like metal in cloth, or books. The man in grey kept the key and said Rennick would have the other. Bram does not yet know about the crossbowman's key; he asked me what I noticed about the men on the road.

player_notes.title: The Salt Barrel
player_notes.text: A cheap, smoky tavern by the wharf where the porters drink. The burglar Pell says a heavy man with a broken nose, stubble, a patched brown coat and a bandaged hand (the brigand who fled the ambush, I think) paid him a half-talent in Cealdish silver there to lift Bram's strongbox from the apothecary's loft. Pell had a tin barrel token for credit. Pell's old master Hobb, a lockmender and fence off Tallow Lane who died two winters ago, is remembered by the old men at the Barrel, who mostly owe him something. Possible contacts. The Wren barge is at the same wharf. Marta warned me to watch myself there: the place has long ears.

player_notes.title: Promise to Marta
player_notes.text: Told Marta the strongbox will most likely bring more trouble, but that I intend to be rid of it tomorrow. Paid her five jots for the trouble, the stitches and the loft. Sergeant Voss wants to see the box with his own eyes before it leaves her yard, and wants a written account from me by noon. Pell, the burglar, is in the cells for a night; if he points out the heavy man at the Salt Barrel and swears to it, he gets a year's service with the watch's locksmith instead of prison.
